title: Frontend: Array Chunking
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Array Chunking. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({values,size}). Return consecutive copied chunks with a possibly shorter final chunk. size must be a positive integer; reject otherwise with Invalid size.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Validate the size before looping so zero or negative values cannot cause an infinite loop.
alternativeApproaches: Implement lazy chunking over an iterable and define whether the final partial chunk is emitted.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty array; size one; size larger than input.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
